analysis:
The only PR change in InstalledSessionCheck.swift is test-only. In localOnlyServing(), the relay test now binds an OS-assigned ephemeral loopback port, via the new ephemeralLoopbackPort() helper (head lines 301-333). The old code derived a port from getpid() in the 47000-47199 range and could collide with cluster ports 47421-47423. The helper asserts the port is not in clusterPorts. Two other hunks (base 806, 820-821) are line-level edits in the portion I could not see, and the patch excerpt is truncated. The visible head units 1-342 and base units 970-1323 show nothing that touches security-relevant behavior.

There is no change to production provider code, coordinator contract, attestation, key custody, the prefix-cache SSD tier (T-041), the add-on hold socket, or any other threat-model asset or trust boundary. The relay still binds 127.0.0.1 only. The change adds a small test-only TOCTOU: the probe socket is closed before the relay re-binds the port, but ClusterLocalRelay(port:) is retried up to 8 times, so this is a flakiness concern, not a security one. It also reduces the chance that a test collides with or interferes with a live pair's listeners on the same Mac.

I did not see ClusterLocalRelay, ClusterLocalServing, or the real-hunk contents beyond the excerpt. Nothing in the supplied evidence suggests a regression, and this unit is a test file that does not ship in the provider artifact. Integration needs no follow-up on this unit.
